title: IB Computer Science Exam Papers: Final-Weeks Plan
summary: IB Computer Science exam papers become a final-weeks system: practise under time, mark precisely, log errors, and repair weak topics with daily focus.
body_markdown:
The final weeks of IB Computer Science revision are not about completing the largest possible pile of exam papers. They are about turning each attempt into evidence: where time disappears, which command terms you misread, and what the markscheme expects that your answer does not yet provide.


A strong routine is simple. Sit a paper under realistic conditions, mark it honestly, record every meaningful error, repair the underlying topic, and attempt a similar question several days later. That final step matters. Without it, reviewing a mistake can create the comforting illusion that the mistake has been fixed.


One detail must come first. Make sure every resource matches your assessment session. The previous IB Computer Science course has its final assessment in November 2026, while the redesigned course has its first assessment in May 2027. The newer course uses Paper 1 for concepts and the case study, while Paper 2 focuses on computational thinking and problem solving. Do not build your final-weeks plan around a format that you will not sit.


### The final-weeks checklist


Use this cycle for every substantial practice session:


- Choose a syllabus-matched paper or focused question set.
- Attempt it without notes and within a fixed time.
- Mark each response against the IB Computer Science markscheme.
- Label the reason for every lost mark.
- Relearn only the weak concepts revealed by the attempt.
- Complete targeted questions on those concepts.
- Revisit the original errors after 2-4 days.
- Finish each week with a fresh timed paper in Exam mode.


This is less dramatic than rereading an entire textbook. It is also far more useful, because the paper decides what you study next.


### Begin with a diagnostic attempt


Your first timed attempt is not a verdict on your final grade. It is a map.


Choose a complete paper appropriate to your level and syllabus. Recreate exam conditions as closely as practical: clear desk, permitted equipment only, no notifications, and no checking notes halfway through. If you run out of time, stop when the allocated time ends. The unfinished questions reveal something important about pacing.


Record the time at a few checkpoints. You do not need to watch the clock after every sentence, but you should know whether one extended response or algorithm consumed a disproportionate share of the session.


Students who need a broader refresher before this first attempt can use the[IB Computer Science last-minute study guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-pass-ib-computer-science-in-1-week-last-minute-study-guide) . If you are aiming higher rather than simply stabilising your grade, the[guide to earning a 7 in IB Computer Science](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-get-a-7-in-ib-computer-science) offers a useful longer-range perspective.


A student discovers that the bug is hiding in the revision plan


### Mark for understanding, not reassurance


Self-marking is where exam practice either becomes valuable or collapses into wishful thinking.


Read the IB Computer Science markscheme one marking point at a time. Award a mark only when your written answer communicates the required idea. Do not give yourself credit because you were thinking about the right concept. An examiner can assess only what appears on the page.


Use three symbols while marking:


- **M** for missing knowledge.
- **A** for application or explanation that was too vague.
- **T** for a timing or technique problem.


These labels separate different kinds of weakness. A student who cannot define encapsulation needs content review. A student who knows the definition but ignores the scenario needs application practice. A student who leaves the response blank may need a pacing rule rather than another hour of notes.


Pay particular attention to command terms. A definition may earn little credit when the question asks you to explain, compare, evaluate, or construct. The difference is not cosmetic. It changes the structure and depth of the answer.


For more guidance on assessment demands, read[how to master IB Computer Science assessments](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/mastering-ib-computer-science-assessments) . Students following the new course should also review the[2027 Paper 1 case study question guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/2027-ib-computer-science-paper-1-case-study-questions) .


### Build an error log that changes tomorrow's revision


An error log should be brief enough to maintain and specific enough to guide action. A long diary of disappointment will not help. A compact table will.


Question Marks lost because Topic Repair task Retest date


Algorithm trace Updated the variable in the wrong order Algorithms Trace three similar loops by hand Thursday


Network response Listed features without explaining impact Networks Write two developed explanations Friday


Extended answer Ignored the scenario Command terms Annotate context before writing Saturday


Avoid entries such as “careless mistake.” That phrase hides the cause. Did you misread the condition? Skip a trace-table column? Confuse a queue with a stack? Run out of time? Name the behaviour precisely enough that you can design a response to it.


Patterns become visible after two or three sessions. Perhaps your factual recall is secure but your explanations stop one step too early. Perhaps algorithm questions are accurate but slow. Perhaps database terminology disappears under pressure. The log turns a vague feeling of weakness into a finite repair list.


### Repair weak topics with targeted IB Computer Science practice


Once you know the problem, do not immediately sit another full paper. Full papers are good at revealing weaknesses but inefficient at repairing a narrow one.


Use the[RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) to build a short set around the topic you missed. Complete several related questions while the markscheme language is fresh. Then close the solution and explain the concept from memory.


A practical repair sequence looks like this:


1. Read the relevant Study Notes for 10-15 minutes.
2. Use Flashcards to retrieve definitions and distinctions without prompts.
3. Ask AI Chat to clarify a step you genuinely do not understand.
4. Complete 3-5 focused questions in the Questionbank.
5. Use grading tools to compare your response with markscheme expectations.
6. Return to the original question after a delay.


RevisionDojo's[Computer Science flashcards](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-computer-science-new/flashcards) are useful for quick retrieval sessions. If terminology is repeatedly costing marks, use the[guide to memorising Computer Science definitions](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-memorize-ib-computer-science-definitions-and-terms-fast) . For algorithmic work, the explanation of[computational thinking in IB Computer Science](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-computational-thinking-in-ib-computer-science) helps connect individual techniques to the larger problem-solving process.


The purpose is not to consume every resource. RevisionDojo brings Questionbank practice, Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, grading tools, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, the Coursework Library, and Tutors into one place, but the error log should determine which tool you open next.


### Alternate targeted work with timed papers


A useful final-weeks rhythm alternates repair and simulation.


Day Main task


Monday Timed paper and honest self-marking


Tuesday Repair the two highest-value weak topics


Wednesday Targeted Questionbank session


Thursday Retest logged errors without notes


Friday Timed section or algorithm set


Weekend Full paper in Exam mode, followed by review


As the exam approaches, increase realism rather than volume. Sit at the time of day when your examination is scheduled if possible. Practise moving on when a question stalls. Leave enough time to check algorithms, units, labels, and unanswered subparts.


Predicted Papers and Mock Exams can provide fresh material once familiar questions stop measuring genuine recall. However, realism does not mean panic. One carefully reviewed paper is worth more than three rushed attempts followed by a glance at the total mark.


### Turn the final paper into a rehearsal


In the last few days, avoid rebuilding your entire knowledge base. Sit one final realistic paper, mark it, and repair only the most likely sources of avoidable loss. Revisit your error log and look for entries that appear more than once.


By now, the story should have changed. The first attempt told you where marks were leaking. The markscheme showed what complete answers looked like. The Questionbank gave you concentrated IB Computer Science practice, and delayed retesting showed whether the improvement remained.


That is how exam papers become marks. Not through exposure alone, but through a repeated loop of attempt, evidence, repair, and return. Practise weak areas in RevisionDojo's Questionbank, then sit your final timed papers in Exam mode. The final weeks are short, but a short period guided by honest feedback can still be remarkably productive.
